summary: Ask, with the token alone, before a model goes on the card during a rental: may it? The coordinator reads the card afresh - never an answer it kept - and approves the model when its need (`model.need_mib`, the application's own estimate; null adds nothing) and the margin the coordinator keeps free beside it (`limits.margin_mib` on `/state`, 256 MiB unless it was started with another) fit in the card's free memory. Otherwise it refuses in words and numbers - `no_room` when the card has not the room now, `never_fits` when the model would not fit even an empty card - and `memory` says what was needed, the margin, what the card had free and the whole card, never who holds the rest. A card the coordinator cannot read decides nothing: the model is approved, and `memory` says the card was not read (null). Right after a process of the rental has gone, its memory is still coming back: an amend that finds no room then reads the card again until the model fits, for at most `limits.amend_settle_s` after the process went (5 s unless the coordinator was started with another), and only then refuses. `processes`, when sent, is the rental's whole list, as a heartbeat names it, and is applied first - so a process that has just gone is known to be gone before the card is judged; an amend renews nothing. Approved, the rental's `models` follow what is on the card: the models its named processes run, and this one. An amend on a rental that is over is refused with the reason, as a heartbeat is, and a ticket that holds no rental is `not_held`. WHILE THE RENTAL IS DEGRADED (the card over-full: its free memory read under the floor, or a model's log said the memory ran out - `rental.degraded`) nothing new goes on the card: an amend is refused `degraded`, saying why, until the coordinator's look at the card finds it has room again.
